Presidential birth places, birth dates, death dates and location where each U.S. President died.John Adams Birthplace
John Adams was born on October 30, 1735 in what was Braintree (now Quincy), Massachusetts in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the Adams National Historic Park. It is open to the public to visit.
George Washington Birthplace
George Washington was born on February 22, 1732 in Westmoreland County, Virginia at his family's Popes Creek plantation home. The house in which he was born was destroyed in a fire in 1779. The property is now part of the George Washington Birthplace National Monument and is open to the public to visit.
Scranton, Pennsylvania
Joe Biden was born at St. Mary's Hospital in Scranton, Pennsylvania. The original building shown in the photographs above is currently a school.
Caldwell, New Jersey
Grover Cleveland was born on March 18, 1837 in Caldwell, New Jersey in the home of his parents. His father was a Presbyterian minister in Caldwell at the time and the house provided for the pastor was referred to as a manse. The original building is now part of the Grover Cleveland Birthplace State Historic Site. It is open to the public to visit.
Cincinnati, Ohio
William Howard Taft was born on September 15, 1857 in Cincinnati, Ohio in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the William Howard Taft National Historic Site. It is free and open to the public to visit.
Point Pleasant, Ohio
Ulysses S. Grant was born on April 27, 1822 in Point Pleasant, Ohio in the home that his parents were renting. The original house was moved to various locations before returning to its original site in 1936. The site is owned by the State of Ohio (Ohio Historical Society) and is open to the public to visit.

 These lists give the

Birthplaces[edit]Twenty-one states have the distinction of being the birthplace of a president. 
One president's birth state is in dispute; North and South Carolina (British colonies at the time) both lay claim to 
Andrew Jackson, who was born in 1767 in the 
Waxhaw region along their common border. Jackson himself considered South Carolina his birth state.

British subject).

Virginia dynasty is sometimes used to describe the fact that four of the first five U.S. presidents were from Virginia.

Presidential birth places, birth dates, death dates and location where each U.S. President died.John Adams Birthplace
John Adams was born on October 30, 1735 in what was Braintree (now Quincy), Massachusetts in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the Adams National Historic Park. It is open to the public to visit.
George Washington Birthplace
George Washington was born on February 22, 1732 in Westmoreland County, Virginia at his family's Popes Creek plantation home. The house in which he was born was destroyed in a fire in 1779. The property is now part of the George Washington Birthplace National Monument and is open to the public to visit.
Scranton, Pennsylvania
Joe Biden was born at St. Mary's Hospital in Scranton, Pennsylvania. The original building shown in the photographs above is currently a school.
Caldwell, New Jersey
Grover Cleveland was born on March 18, 1837 in Caldwell, New Jersey in the home of his parents. His father was a Presbyterian minister in Caldwell at the time and the house provided for the pastor was referred to as a manse. The original building is now part of the Grover Cleveland Birthplace State Historic Site. It is open to the public to visit.
Cincinnati, Ohio
William Howard Taft was born on September 15, 1857 in Cincinnati, Ohio in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the William Howard Taft National Historic Site. It is free and open to the public to visit.
Point Pleasant, Ohio
Ulysses S. Grant was born on April 27, 1822 in Point Pleasant, Ohio in the home that his parents were renting. The original house was moved to various locations before returning to its original site in 1936. The site is owned by the State of Ohio (Ohio Historical Society) and is open to the public to visit.

The Wikipedia page lists the birthplaces of U.S. presidents along with their respective birth states. Presidents have been born in 21 different states, with Virginia (8) and Ohio (7) leading in numbers. George Washington was born in Popes Creek, Virginia; John Adams in Braintree, Massachusetts; Thomas Jefferson in Shadwell, Virginia; and James Madison in Port Conway, Virginia, among others. Notably, Andrew Jackson's birthplace is contested between North and South Carolina, with Jackson himself asserting South Carolina as his birth state. Some presidents like Martin Van Buren marked the transition by being the first president born as an American citizen instead of a British subject.

The table provided categorizes presidents by name, date of birth, birthplace, and state of birth, from George Washington born in Virginia to Joe Biden born in Scranton, Pennsylvania. Notable cities include Honolulu, Hawaii for Barack Obama and New York, New York for Donald Trump. The page also notes preserved birthplaces as historic sites, reflecting the significance and heritage of these locations.

The Wikipedia page lists the birthplaces of U.S. presidents along with their respective birth states. Presidents have been born in 21 different states, with Virginia (8) and Ohio (7) leading in numbers. George Washington was born in Popes Creek, Virginia; John Adams in Braintree, Massachusetts; Thomas Jefferson in Shadwell, Virginia; and James Madison in Port Conway, Virginia, among others. Notably, Andrew Jackson's birthplace is contested between North and South Carolina, with Jackson himself asserting South Carolina as his birth state. Some presidents like Martin Van Buren marked the transition by being the first president born as an American citizen instead of a British subject.

The table provided categorizes presidents by name, date of birth, birthplace, and state of birth, from George Washington born in Virginia to Joe Biden born in Scranton, Pennsylvania. Notable cities include Honolulu, Hawaii for Barack Obama and New York, New York for Donald Trump. The page also notes preserved birthplaces as historic sites, reflecting the significance and heritage of these locations.

With the list of presidential birthplaces obtained, write a Python script to calculate the distances between these cities. Start by gathering the coordinates for each city using a geocoding service, then calculate the geodesic distances to find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

message.content:
To compute the distances between the cities, we'll first gather the geographical coordinates for each city using a geocoding service like OpenCage Geocoding API. After obtaining the coordinates, we'll calculate the geodesic distances using the `geopy` library.

Here's a Python script to perform these tasks:

### Steps

1. **Collect Coordinates**: Use the OpenCage Geocoding API to get the coordinates for each city.
2. **Calculate Distances**: Use the `geopy` library to compute geodesic distances.
3. **Identify Required Cities**: Find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

### Script
Ensure you have your OpenCage API key, and have installed `geopy` and `requests`:

```bash
pip install geopy requests
```

### Python Code
```python
import requests
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# Sample list of presidential birthplaces (City, State)
presidential_birthplaces = [
    ("Popes Creek", "Virginia"),
    ("Braintree", "Massachusetts"),
    ("Shadwell", "Virginia"),
    ("Port Conway", "Virginia"),
    ("Waxhaw", "South Carolina"),
    ("Kinderhook", "New York"),
    ("Honolulu", "Hawaii"),
    # Add more cities from your list
]

# Function to get coordinates using OpenCage API
def get_coordinates(city, state, api_key):
    url = f"https://api.opencagedata.com/geocode/v1/json?q={city},{state}&key={api_key}"
    response = requests.get(url).json()
    if response["results"]:
        return response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lat"], response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lng"]
    else:
        return None

# Your OpenCage API Key
API_KEY = 'your_opencage_api_key_here'

# Collect coordinates
city_coordinates = {}
for city, state in presidential_birthplaces:
    coords = get_coordinates(city, state, API_KEY)
    if coords:
        city_coordinates[(city, state)] = coords

# Calculate distances and find farthest cities
westernmost_city = min(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]
easternmost_city = max(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]

# Output the result
farthest_cities = sorted([westernmost_city[0], easternmost_city[0]])
result = ", ".join(farthest_cities)

print("## ANSWER")
print(result)
print("## REASON")
print(f"The westernmost city is {westernmost_city[0]}, and the easternmost city is {easternmost_city[0]}.")
```

### Instructions
1. Replace `'your_opencage_api_key_here'` with your actual OpenCage API key.
2. Add all the presidential birthplaces to the `presidential_birthplaces` list.
3. Run the script to get the answer.

This script will calculate and print the result directly. Run it using a Python interpreter to get the final output.

Presidential birth places, birth dates, death dates and location where each U.S. President died.John Adams Birthplace
John Adams was born on October 30, 1735 in what was Braintree (now Quincy), Massachusetts in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the Adams National Historic Park. It is open to the public to visit.
George Washington Birthplace
George Washington was born on February 22, 1732 in Westmoreland County, Virginia at his family's Popes Creek plantation home. The house in which he was born was destroyed in a fire in 1779. The property is now part of the George Washington Birthplace National Monument and is open to the public to visit.
Scranton, Pennsylvania
Joe Biden was born at St. Mary's Hospital in Scranton, Pennsylvania. The original building shown in the photographs above is currently a school.
Caldwell, New Jersey
Grover Cleveland was born on March 18, 1837 in Caldwell, New Jersey in the home of his parents. His father was a Presbyterian minister in Caldwell at the time and the house provided for the pastor was referred to as a manse. The original building is now part of the Grover Cleveland Birthplace State Historic Site. It is open to the public to visit.
Cincinnati, Ohio
William Howard Taft was born on September 15, 1857 in Cincinnati, Ohio in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the William Howard Taft National Historic Site. It is free and open to the public to visit.
Point Pleasant, Ohio
Ulysses S. Grant was born on April 27, 1822 in Point Pleasant, Ohio in the home that his parents were renting. The original house was moved to various locations before returning to its original site in 1936. The site is owned by the State of Ohio (Ohio Historical Society) and is open to the public to visit.

Presidents have been born in 21 different states, with Virginia (8) and Ohio (7) leading in numbers. With the list of presidential birthplaces obtained, write a Python script to calculate the distances between these cities. Start by gathering the coordinates for each city using a geocoding service, then calculate the geodesic distances to find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

To compute the distances between the cities, we'll first gather the geographical coordinates for each city using a geocoding service like OpenCage Geocoding API. After obtaining the coordinates, we'll calculate the geodesic distances using the `geopy` library.

Here's a Python script to perform these tasks:

### Steps

1. **Collect Coordinates**: Use the OpenCage Geocoding API to get the coordinates for each city.
2. **Calculate Distances**: Use the `geopy` library to compute geodesic distances.
3. **Identify Required Cities**: Find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

### Script
Ensure you have your OpenCage API key, and have installed `geopy` and `requests`:

```bash
pip install geopy requests
```

### Python Code
```python
import requests
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# Sample list of presidential birthplaces (City, State)
presidential_birthplaces = [
    ("Popes Creek", "Virginia"),
    ("Braintree", "Massachusetts"),
    ("Shadwell", "Virginia"),
    ("Port Conway", "Virginia"),
    ("Waxhaw", "South Carolina"),
    ("Kinderhook", "New York"),
    ("Honolulu", "Hawaii"),
    # Add more cities from your list
]

# Function to get coordinates using OpenCage API
def get_coordinates(city, state, api_key):
    url = f"https://api.opencagedata.com/geocode/v1/json?q={city},{state}&key={api_key}"
    response = requests.get(url).json()
    if response["results"]:
        return response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lat"], response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lng"]
    else:
        return None

# Your OpenCage API Key
API_KEY = 'your_opencage_api_key_here'

# Collect coordinates
city_coordinates = {}
for city, state in presidential_birthplaces:
    coords = get_coordinates(city, state, API_KEY)
    if coords:
        city_coordinates[(city, state)] = coords

# Calculate distances and find farthest cities
westernmost_city = min(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]
easternmost_city = max(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]

# Output the result
farthest_cities = sorted([westernmost_city[0], easternmost_city[0]])
result = ", ".join(farthest_cities)

print("## ANSWER")
print(result)
print("## REASON")
print(f"The westernmost city is {westernmost_city[0]}, and the easternmost city is {easternmost_city[0]}.")
```

The Wikipedia page lists the birthplaces of U.S. presidents along with their respective birth states. Presidents have been born in 21 different states, with Virginia (8) and Ohio (7) leading in numbers. George Washington was born in Popes Creek, Virginia; John Adams in Braintree, Massachusetts; Thomas Jefferson in Shadwell, Virginia; and James Madison in Port Conway, Virginia, among others. Notably, Andrew Jackson's birthplace is contested between North and South Carolina, with Jackson himself asserting South Carolina as his birth state. Some presidents like Martin Van Buren marked the transition by being the first president born as an American citizen instead of a British subject.

The table provided categorizes presidents by name, date of birth, birthplace, and state of birth, from George Washington born in Virginia to Joe Biden born in Scranton, Pennsylvania. Notable cities include Honolulu, Hawaii for Barack Obama and New York, New York for Donald Trump. The page also notes preserved birthplaces as historic sites, reflecting the significance and heritage of these locations.

With the list of presidential birthplaces obtained, write a Python script to calculate the distances between these cities. Start by gathering the coordinates for each city using a geocoding service, then calculate the geodesic distances to find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

To compute the distances between the cities, we'll first gather the geographical coordinates for each city using a geocoding service like OpenCage Geocoding API. After obtaining the coordinates, we'll calculate the geodesic distances using the `geopy` library.

Here's a Python script to perform these tasks:

### Steps

1. **Collect Coordinates**: Use the OpenCage Geocoding API to get the coordinates for each city.
2. **Calculate Distances**: Use the `geopy` library to compute geodesic distances.
3. **Identify Required Cities**: Find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

### Script
Ensure you have your OpenCage API key, and have installed `geopy` and `requests`:

```bash
pip install geopy requests
```

### Python Code
```python
import requests
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# Sample list of presidential birthplaces (City, State)
presidential_birthplaces = [
    ("Popes Creek", "Virginia"),
    ("Braintree", "Massachusetts"),
    ("Shadwell", "Virginia"),
    ("Port Conway", "Virginia"),
    ("Waxhaw", "South Carolina"),
    ("Kinderhook", "New York"),
    ("Honolulu", "Hawaii"),
    # Add more cities from your list
]

# Function to get coordinates using OpenCage API
def get_coordinates(city, state, api_key):
    url = f"https://api.opencagedata.com/geocode/v1/json?q={city},{state}&key={api_key}"
    response = requests.get(url).json()
    if response["results"]:
        return response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lat"], response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lng"]
    else:
        return None

# Your OpenCage API Key
API_KEY = 'your_opencage_api_key_here'

# Collect coordinates
city_coordinates = {}
for city, state in presidential_birthplaces:
    coords = get_coordinates(city, state, API_KEY)
    if coords:
        city_coordinates[(city, state)] = coords

# Calculate distances and find farthest cities
westernmost_city = min(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]
easternmost_city = max(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]

# Output the result
farthest_cities = sorted([westernmost_city[0], easternmost_city[0]])
result = ", ".join(farthest_cities)

print("## ANSWER")
print(result)
print("## REASON")
print(f"The westernmost city is {westernmost_city[0]}, and the easternmost city is {easternmost_city[0]}.")
```

### Instructions
1. Replace `'your_opencage_api_key_here'` with your actual OpenCage API key.
2. Add all the presidential birthplaces to the `presidential_birthplaces` list.
3. Run the script to get the answer.

The Wikipedia page lists the birthplaces of U.S. presidents along with their respective birth states. Presidents have been born in 21 different states, with Virginia (8) and Ohio (7) leading in numbers. George Washington was born in Popes Creek, Virginia; John Adams in Braintree, Massachusetts; Thomas Jefferson in Shadwell, Virginia; and James Madison in Port Conway, Virginia, among others. Notably, Andrew Jackson's birthplace is contested between North and South Carolina, with Jackson himself asserting South Carolina as his birth state. Some presidents like Martin Van Buren marked the transition by being the first president born as an American citizen instead of a British subject.

The table provided categorizes presidents by name, date of birth, birthplace, and state of birth, from George Washington born in Virginia to Joe Biden born in Scranton, Pennsylvania. Notable cities include Honolulu, Hawaii for Barack Obama and New York, New York for Donald Trump. The page also notes preserved birthplaces as historic sites, reflecting the significance and heritage of these locations.

With the list of presidential birthplaces obtained, write a Python script to calculate the distances between these cities. Start by gathering the coordinates for each city using a geocoding service, then calculate the geodesic distances to find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

To compute the distances between the cities, we'll first gather the geographical coordinates for each city using a geocoding service like OpenCage Geocoding API. After obtaining the coordinates, we'll calculate the geodesic distances using the `geopy` library.

Here's a Python script to perform these tasks:

### Steps

1. **Collect Coordinates**: Use the OpenCage Geocoding API to get the coordinates for each city.
2. **Calculate Distances**: Use the `geopy` library to compute geodesic distances.
3. **Identify Required Cities**: Find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

### Script
Ensure you have your OpenCage API key, and have installed `geopy` and `requests`:

```bash
pip install geopy requests
```

### Python Code
```python
import requests
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# Sample list of presidential birthplaces (City, State)
presidential_birthplaces = [
    ("Popes Creek", "Virginia"),
    ("Braintree", "Massachusetts"),
    ("Shadwell", "Virginia"),
    ("Port Conway", "Virginia"),
    ("Waxhaw", "South Carolina"),
    ("Kinderhook", "New York"),
    ("Honolulu", "Hawaii"),
    # Add more cities from your list
]

# Function to get coordinates using OpenCage API
def get_coordinates(city, state, api_key):
    url = f"https://api.opencagedata.com/geocode/v1/json?q={city},{state}&key={api_key}"
    response = requests.get(url).json()
    if response["results"]:
        return response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lat"], response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lng"]
    else:
        return None

# Your OpenCage API Key
API_KEY = 'your_opencage_api_key_here'

# Collect coordinates
city_coordinates = {}
for city, state in presidential_birthplaces:
    coords = get_coordinates(city, state, API_KEY)
    if coords:
        city_coordinates[(city, state)] = coords

# Calculate distances and find farthest cities
westernmost_city = min(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]
easternmost_city = max(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]

# Output the result
farthest_cities = sorted([westernmost_city[0], easternmost_city[0]])
result = ", ".join(farthest_cities)

print("## ANSWER")
print(result)
print("## REASON")
print(f"The westernmost city is {westernmost_city[0]}, and the easternmost city is {easternmost_city[0]}.")
```

### Instructions
1. Replace `'your_opencage_api_key_here'` with your actual OpenCage API key.
2. Add all the presidential birthplaces to the `presidential_birthplaces` list.
3. Run the script to get the answer.

Presidential birth places, birth dates, death dates and location where each U.S. President died.John Adams Birthplace
John Adams was born on October 30, 1735 in what was Braintree (now Quincy), Massachusetts in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the Adams National Historic Park. It is open to the public to visit.
George Washington Birthplace
George Washington was born on February 22, 1732 in Westmoreland County, Virginia at his family's Popes Creek plantation home. The house in which he was born was destroyed in a fire in 1779. The property is now part of the George Washington Birthplace National Monument and is open to the public to visit.
Scranton, Pennsylvania
Joe Biden was born at St. Mary's Hospital in Scranton, Pennsylvania. The original building shown in the photographs above is currently a school.
Caldwell, New Jersey
Grover Cleveland was born on March 18, 1837 in Caldwell, New Jersey in the home of his parents. His father was a Presbyterian minister in Caldwell at the time and the house provided for the pastor was referred to as a manse. The original building is now part of the Grover Cleveland Birthplace State Historic Site. It is open to the public to visit.
Cincinnati, Ohio
William Howard Taft was born on September 15, 1857 in Cincinnati, Ohio in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the William Howard Taft National Historic Site. It is free and open to the public to visit.
Point Pleasant, Ohio
Ulysses S. Grant was born on April 27, 1822 in Point Pleasant, Ohio in the home that his parents were renting. The original house was moved to various locations before returning to its original site in 1936. The site is owned by the State of Ohio (Ohio Historical Society) and is open to the public to visit.

messages.content: Extract the list of presidents and their birthplaces from the webpage. We need the specific cities and states for calculation of the distances.

The Wikipedia page lists the birthplaces of U.S. presidents along with their respective birth states. Presidents have been born in 21 different states, with Virginia (8) and Ohio (7) leading in numbers. George Washington was born in Popes Creek, Virginia; John Adams in Braintree, Massachusetts; Thomas Jefferson in Shadwell, Virginia; and James Madison in Port Conway, Virginia, among others. Notably, Andrew Jackson's birthplace is contested between North and South Carolina, with Jackson himself asserting South Carolina as his birth state. Some presidents like Martin Van Buren marked the transition by being the first president born as an American citizen instead of a British subject.

The table provided categorizes presidents by name, date of birth, birthplace, and state of birth, from George Washington born in Virginia to Joe Biden born in Scranton, Pennsylvania. Notable cities include Honolulu, Hawaii for Barack Obama and New York, New York for Donald Trump. The page also notes preserved birthplaces as historic sites, reflecting the significance and heritage of these locations.

With the list of presidential birthplaces obtained, write a Python script to calculate the distances between these cities. Start by gathering the coordinates for each city using a geocoding service, then calculate the geodesic distances to find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

To compute the distances between the cities, we'll first gather the geographical coordinates for each city using a geocoding service like OpenCage Geocoding API. After obtaining the coordinates, we'll calculate the geodesic distances using the `geopy` library.

Here's a Python script to perform these tasks:

### Steps

1. **Collect Coordinates**: Use the OpenCage Geocoding API to get the coordinates for each city.
2. **Calculate Distances**: Use the `geopy` library to compute geodesic distances.
3. **Identify Required Cities**: Find the westernmost and easternmost cities.

### Script
Ensure you have your OpenCage API key, and have installed `geopy` and `requests`:

```bash
pip install geopy requests
```

### Python Code
```python
import requests
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# Sample list of presidential birthplaces (City, State)
presidential_birthplaces = [
    ("Popes Creek", "Virginia"),
    ("Braintree", "Massachusetts"),
    ("Shadwell", "Virginia"),
    ("Port Conway", "Virginia"),
    ("Waxhaw", "South Carolina"),
    ("Kinderhook", "New York"),
    ("Honolulu", "Hawaii"),
    # Add more cities from your list
]

# Function to get coordinates using OpenCage API
def get_coordinates(city, state, api_key):
    url = f"https://api.opencagedata.com/geocode/v1/json?q={city},{state}&key={api_key}"
    response = requests.get(url).json()
    if response["results"]:
        return response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lat"], response["results"][0]["geometry"]["lng"]
    else:
        return None

# Your OpenCage API Key
API_KEY = 'your_opencage_api_key_here'

# Collect coordinates
city_coordinates = {}
for city, state in presidential_birthplaces:
    coords = get_coordinates(city, state, API_KEY)
    if coords:
        city_coordinates[(city, state)] = coords

# Calculate distances and find farthest cities
westernmost_city = min(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]
easternmost_city = max(city_coordinates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][1])[0]

# Output the result
farthest_cities = sorted([westernmost_city[0], easternmost_city[0]])
result = ", ".join(farthest_cities)

print("## ANSWER")
print(result)
print("## REASON")
print(f"The westernmost city is {westernmost_city[0]}, and the easternmost city is {easternmost_city[0]}.")
```

### Instructions
1. Replace `'your_opencage_api_key_here'` with your actual OpenCage API key.
2. Add all the presidential birthplaces to the `presidential_birthplaces` list.
3. Run the script to get the answer.

Presidential birth places, birth dates, death dates and location where each U.S. President died.John Adams Birthplace
John Adams was born on October 30, 1735 in what was Braintree (now Quincy), Massachusetts in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the Adams National Historic Park. It is open to the public to visit.
George Washington Birthplace
George Washington was born on February 22, 1732 in Westmoreland County, Virginia at his family's Popes Creek plantation home. The house in which he was born was destroyed in a fire in 1779. The property is now part of the George Washington Birthplace National Monument and is open to the public to visit.
Scranton, Pennsylvania
Joe Biden was born at St. Mary's Hospital in Scranton, Pennsylvania. The original building shown in the photographs above is currently a school.
Caldwell, New Jersey
Grover Cleveland was born on March 18, 1837 in Caldwell, New Jersey in the home of his parents. His father was a Presbyterian minister in Caldwell at the time and the house provided for the pastor was referred to as a manse. The original building is now part of the Grover Cleveland Birthplace State Historic Site. It is open to the public to visit.
Cincinnati, Ohio
William Howard Taft was born on September 15, 1857 in Cincinnati, Ohio in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the William Howard Taft National Historic Site. It is free and open to the public to visit.
Point Pleasant, Ohio
Ulysses S. Grant was born on April 27, 1822 in Point Pleasant, Ohio in the home that his parents were renting. The original house was moved to various locations before returning to its original site in 1936. The site is owned by the State of Ohio (Ohio Historical Society) and is open to the public to visit.

import requests

Presidential birth places, birth dates, death dates and location where each U.S. President died.John Adams Birthplace
John Adams was born on October 30, 1735 in what was Braintree (now Quincy), Massachusetts in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the Adams National Historic Park. It is open to the public to visit.
George Washington Birthplace
George Washington was born on February 22, 1732 in Westmoreland County, Virginia at his family's Popes Creek plantation home. The house in which he was born was destroyed in a fire in 1779. The property is now part of the George Washington Birthplace National Monument and is open to the public to visit.
Scranton, Pennsylvania
Joe Biden was born at St. Mary's Hospital in Scranton, Pennsylvania. The original building shown in the photographs above is currently a school.
Caldwell, New Jersey
Grover Cleveland was born on March 18, 1837 in Caldwell, New Jersey in the home of his parents. His father was a Presbyterian minister in Caldwell at the time and the house provided for the pastor was referred to as a manse. The original building is now part of the Grover Cleveland Birthplace State Historic Site. It is open to the public to visit.
Cincinnati, Ohio
William Howard Taft was born on September 15, 1857 in Cincinnati, Ohio in the home of his parents. The original house is now part of the William Howard Taft National Historic Site. It is free and open to the public to visit.
Point Pleasant, Ohio
Ulysses S. Grant was born on April 27, 1822 in Point Pleasant, Ohio in the home that his parents were renting. The original house was moved to various locations before returning to its original site in 1936. The site is owned by the State of Ohio (Ohio Historical Society) and is open to the public to visit.

To proceed with calculating distances between the cities where U.S. presidents were born, let's follow these steps:

### Plan

1. **Obtain Coordinates:**
   - We'll use `geopy` to get geographical coordinates for each city obtained from the list.

2. **Calculate Distances:**
   - Calculate the geodesic distances between these cities to identify the westernmost and easternmost cities.

3. **Determine the Farthest Cities:**
   - Identify the two cities that are farthest apart from west to east.

### Preparation and Execution Steps

#### Step 1: Install Required Libraries

Let's install the required Python libraries: `geopy`.

```sh
pip install geopy
```

#### Step 2: Script for Obtaining Coordinates and Calculating Distances

Here is a script that will find the westernmost and easternmost birthplaces and calculate the distances:

```python
from geopy.geocoders import Nominatim
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# List of U.S. presidents' birthplaces
birthplaces = [
    "Westmoreland Co., Va.", "Quincy, Mass.", "Albemarle Co., Va.", 
    "Port Conway, Va.", "Westmoreland Co., Va.", "Quincy, Mass.", 
    "Waxhaws, No/So Carolina", "Kinderhook, New York", "Charles City Co., Va.", 
    "Charles City Co., Va.", "Mecklenburg Co., N.C.", "Orange County, Va.", 
    "Cayuga Co., New York", "Hillsborough, N.H.", "Cove Gap, Pa."
]

# Function to get the coordinates of a place
def get_coordinates(place):
    geolocator = Nominatim(user_agent="geoapi")
    location = geolocator.geocode(place)
    return (location.latitude, location.longitude) if location else None

# Get coordinates for each birthplace
coordinates = {place: get_coordinates(place) for place in birthplaces}

westernmost_city = None
easternmost_city = None
max_distance = 0

# Compare each city
for place1, coord1 in coordinates.items():
    if coord1:
        for place2, coord2 in coordinates.items():
            if coord2 and place1 != place2:
                distance = geodesic(coord1, coord2).km
                if distance > max_distance:
                    max_distance = distance
                    westernmost_city, easternmost_city = place1, place2

# Sort cities alphabetically
final_cities = sorted([westernmost_city, easternmost_city])

print("Westernmost City:", westernmost_city)
print("Easternmost City:", easternmost_city)
print("Farthest Cities Alphabetically:", ", ".join(final_cities))
```

#### Final Step: Analyze Output

- Once the script runs, review the output to verify the two cities that are the farthest apart.
- Ensure the names of the cities are displayed in alphabetical order.

The webpage "U.S. Presidents Birthplaces and Location of Death" provides a comprehensive list detailing all U.S. presidents' birth and death information, including dates and locations. It includes an interactive feature allowing users to view photographs of the birthplaces by clicking the location links. Additionally, the page offers resources to explore the presidents’ birthplaces by state and includes a link to view their gravesites. The page is managed by Baaron's Hill, LLC with a focus on historical education.

For further exploration, the page offers buttons to access a photo gallery of presidential birthplaces and to view the birthplaces by state. There is an emphasis on educational engagement by linking to photos of the various sites, enhancing the historical understanding and connection to America's presidential heritage.

Use the list of U.S. presidents' birthplaces to obtain their geographical coordinates, focusing on detecting the cities farthest apart from west to east. Incorporate error handling and prepare to utilize geopy or similar tools for distance calculation.

To proceed with calculating distances between the cities where U.S. presidents were born, let's follow these steps:

### Plan

1. **Obtain Coordinates:**
   - We'll use `geopy` to get geographical coordinates for each city obtained from the list.

2. **Calculate Distances:**
   - Calculate the geodesic distances between these cities to identify the westernmost and easternmost cities.

3. **Determine the Farthest Cities:**
   - Identify the two cities that are farthest apart from west to east.

### Preparation and Execution Steps

#### Step 1: Install Required Libraries

Let's install the required Python libraries: `geopy`.

```sh
pip install geopy
```

#### Step 2: Script for Obtaining Coordinates and Calculating Distances

Here is a script that will find the westernmost and easternmost birthplaces and calculate the distances:

```python
from geopy.geocoders import Nominatim
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# List of U.S. presidents' birthplaces
birthplaces = [
    "Westmoreland Co., Va.", "Quincy, Mass.", "Albemarle Co., Va.", 
    "Port Conway, Va.", "Westmoreland Co., Va.", "Quincy, Mass.", 
    "Waxhaws, No/So Carolina", "Kinderhook, New York", "Charles City Co., Va.", 
    "Charles City Co., Va.", "Mecklenburg Co., N.C.", "Orange County, Va.", 
    "Cayuga Co., New York", "Hillsborough, N.H.", "Cove Gap, Pa."
]

# Function to get the coordinates of a place
def get_coordinates(place):
    geolocator = Nominatim(user_agent="geoapi")
    location = geolocator.geocode(place)
    return (location.latitude, location.longitude) if location else None

# Get coordinates for each birthplace
coordinates = {place: get_coordinates(place) for place in birthplaces}

westernmost_city = None
easternmost_city = None
max_distance = 0

# Compare each city
for place1, coord1 in coordinates.items():
    if coord1:
        for place2, coord2 in coordinates.items():
            if coord2 and place1 != place2:
                distance = geodesic(coord1, coord2).km
                if distance > max_distance:
                    max_distance = distance
                    westernmost_city, easternmost_city = place1, place2

# Sort cities alphabetically
final_cities = sorted([westernmost_city, easternmost_city])

print("Westernmost City:", westernmost_city)
print("Easternmost City:", easternmost_city)
print("Farthest Cities Alphabetically:", ", ".join(final_cities))
```

#### Final Step: Analyze Output

- Once the script runs, review the output to verify the two cities that are the farthest apart.
- Ensure the names of the cities are displayed in alphabetical order.

To proceed with calculating distances between the cities where U.S. presidents were born, let's follow these steps:

### Plan

1. **Obtain Coordinates:**
   - We'll use `geopy` to get geographical coordinates for each city obtained from the list.

2. **Calculate Distances:**
   - Calculate the geodesic distances between these cities to identify the westernmost and easternmost cities.

3. **Determine the Farthest Cities:**
   - Identify the two cities that are farthest apart from west to east.

### Preparation and Execution Steps

#### Step 1: Install Required Libraries

Let's install the required Python libraries: `geopy`.

```sh
pip install geopy
```

#### Step 2: Script for Obtaining Coordinates and Calculating Distances

Here is a script that will find the westernmost and easternmost birthplaces and calculate the distances:

```python
from geopy.geocoders import Nominatim
from geopy.distance import geodesic

# List of U.S. presidents' birthplaces
birthplaces = [
    "Westmoreland Co., Va.", "Quincy, Mass.", "Albemarle Co., Va.", 
    "Port Conway, Va.", "Westmoreland Co., Va.", "Quincy, Mass.", 
    "Waxhaws, No/So Carolina", "Kinderhook, New York", "Charles City Co., Va.", 
    "Charles City Co., Va.", "Mecklenburg Co., N.C.", "Orange County, Va.", 
    "Cayuga Co., New York", "Hillsborough, N.H.", "Cove Gap, Pa."
]

# Function to get the coordinates of a place
def get_coordinates(place):
    geolocator = Nominatim(user_agent="geoapi")
    location = geolocator.geocode(place)
    return (location.latitude, location.longitude) if location else None

# Get coordinates for each birthplace
coordinates = {place: get_coordinates(place) for place in birthplaces}

westernmost_city = None
easternmost_city = None
max_distance = 0

# Compare each city
for place1, coord1 in coordinates.items():
    if coord1:
        for place2, coord2 in coordinates.items():
            if coord2 and place1 != place2:
                distance = geodesic(coord1, coord2).km
                if distance > max_distance:
                    max_distance = distance
                    westernmost_city, easternmost_city = place1, place2

# Sort cities alphabetically
final_cities = sorted([westernmost_city, easternmost_city])

print("Westernmost City:", westernmost_city)
print("Easternmost City:", easternmost_city)
print("Farthest Cities Alphabetically:", ", ".join(final_cities))
```

#### Final Step: Analyze Output

- Once the script runs, review the output to verify the two cities that are the farthest apart.
- Ensure the names of the cities are displayed in alphabetical order.
